compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

On the AGENTIC path the growing tool-result history is re-sent UNCACHED every turn, so input cost
grows O(N^2) in turns — and rebar's own telemetry cannot see it.

`capabilities.py:333-355` `cache_settings_for` sets exactly two of the four available breakpoints:

    anthropic_cache_instructions=True
    anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True

and its docstring says so outright: "neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched."
Applied once at `runner.py:394`.

BOTH UNUSED KNOBS ALREADY EXIST in the pinned dependency — verified by introspection against the
repo's own `.venv` at pydantic-ai 1.107.1, not from docs:

    AnthropicModelSettings: anthropic_cache, anthropic_cache_instructions,
                            anthropic_cache_messages, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions
    BedrockModelSettings:   bedrock_cache_instructions, bedrock_cache_messages,
                            bedrock_cache_tool_definitions

## The failure, concretely

`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250` (`config.py:127`) yields `request_limit = 125`
(`structured_run.py:331`). The agentic Pass-1 criteria and container calls
(`plan_review/passes.py:330, 434`) run a tool loop in which EVERY turn re-sends the full accumulated
message history. With only a system breakpoint that history is never written to cache and never read.
On a 40-turn review whose file-read tool results average 2k tokens, turn 40 re-sends ~80k uncached
tokens that turn 39 also sent.

IT IS INVISIBLE TO OUR TELEMETRY. `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) requires
`cache_read_tokens == 0`, but the SYSTEM block IS hitting cache, so the counter is nonzero and the
predicate never fires. We would never learn this from a usage log.

## Consensus — this is the documented multi-turn shape, not an exotic optimisation

* Anthropic's prompt-caching doc recommends TWO breakpoints for multi-turn: system AND "the final
  block of the final message... so the conversation can be incrementally cached", and names automatic
  caching the "recommended starting point" for multi-turn.
* LangChain's `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`
  (`libs/partners/anthropic/langchain_anthropic/middleware/prompt_caching.py`) tags system + last tool
  and delegates the tail to `model_settings["cache_control"]`.
* pydantic-ai's own Anthropic docs recommend the same triple.
System-only is the documented minimum for a STATIC-PROMPT workload; it is not the shape for an agent.

Corroborating that this was once in scope and got dropped: story REB-458 is titled "Prompt caching at
the shared runner seam (CachePoint + anthropic_cache_*, provider-safe)" and is marked Done, but the
shipped `cache_settings_for` sets two of four knobs and no CachePoint.

## Approach

Thread the execution mode into `cache_settings_for` and, for `agentic` ONLY, add
`anthropic_cache=True` on the Anthropic arm and `bedrock_cache_messages=True` on the Bedrock arm.

MIND THE PROVIDER ASYMMETRY — this is the trap: Bedrock has NO `bedrock_cache` automatic key. LangChain
hit exactly this (langchain#37042): `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware` regressed on Bedrock in 1.4.1
because it switched to top-level automatic caching, which Bedrock rejects with
`cache_control: Extra inputs are not permitted`. So the two arms need different keys, not one shared
setting.

Breakpoint budget is safe: pydantic-ai's `_limit_cache_points()` sets
`MAX_CACHE_POINTS = 3 if automatic_caching else 4`, and this change puts rebar at 3.

Single-turn paths must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL — that is the regression risk and the thing to pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On the AGENTIC path the message tail is cached: a captured multi-turn request shows a breakpoint
      after the accumulated history, and a live run records nonzero `cache_read_tokens` attributable to
      the message tail rather than only to the system block.
- [ ] The Anthropic and Bedrock arms use their OWN keys (`anthropic_cache` vs
      `bedrock_cache_messages`); a test pins that the Bedrock arm never receives a top-level
      `cache_control`, since Bedrock rejects it outright.
- [ ] SINGLE-TURN paths are unchanged, proven by a captured request diff that is byte-identical before
      and after — this is the regression this change could plausibly cause.
- [ ] The cost effect is MEASURED on a real multi-turn agentic run, before and after, and recorded.
      A narrowly-scoped live run is sufficient and is preferred over any eval sweep.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the Config-read
      and env-vars drift gates both pass.
compiled_state.title: Agentic message tail is re-sent uncached every turn: O(N^2) input cost, invisible to our telemetry
